title: Iron Solutions
subtitle: Oral / parenteral iron — anaemia of various causes
content:
[DIAGNOSIS]
- Pallor, fatigue, breathlessness, dizziness
- Lab: Low haemoglobin, low ferritin, low MCV (microcytic)
- Rule out occult blood loss before starting iron

[INVESTIGATIONS]
- Lab: FBC (haemoglobin, MCV low), ferritin (low in iron deficiency), iron studies, B12/folate
- Special test: FOBT (faecal occult blood) or colonoscopy if occult GI bleeding suspected (men/postmenopausal)
- Monitor: Hb response (rise ~1g/dL in 2-4 weeks), ferritin repletion, GI side effects of oral iron
- Screen: Underlying cause — GI source, menstrual loss, malabsorption (coeliac)

[TREATMENT]
- Oral iron is first line for most cases
- Parenteral iron (IV) only if oral fails or not tolerated
- Combine with vitamin C for better absorption
- Avoid concurrent intake with PPIs, tea, milk, or calcium

[WARNING]
Iron overdose is dangerous — keep away from children. Do not exceed recommended dose.
Iron stains teeth — use a straw for liquid forms.

[RX]
- Ferrograd C tab (Ferrous Sulphate + Ascorbic Acid) | قرص واحد يوميًا على معدة فارغة مع كوب ماء | 45 ج.م
- OR Ferrous Sulphate 325mg tab (Ferrous Sulphate) | قرص مرتين إلى 3 مرات يوميًا بعد الأكل | 15 ج.م
- OR Iron sucrose vial (Iron Sucrose) | حقن وريدي حسب تعليمات الطبيب | 85 ج.م
- Vitamin C 500mg tab (Ascorbic Acid) | قرص مرة يوميًا مع الحديد | 12 ج.م
perDrugAlternatives:
Ferrograd C tab (Ferrous Sulphate + Ascorbic Acid) | 45 ج.م: Ferrograd Forte tab | 60 ج.م, Fumafer Plus tab | 30 ج.م, Ferrous Sulphate Arrow tab | 20 ج.م
Ferrous Sulphate 325mg tab | 15 ج.م: Ferrous Sulphate GPO tab | 10 ج.م, Ferrous Fumarate 325mg tab | 18 ج.م, Iron Plus tab | 22 ج.م
Iron sucrose vial | 85 ج.م: Ferrlecit vial | 120 ج.م, Monofer vial | 200 ج.م, Venofer vial | 150 ج.م
Vitamin C 500mg tab | 12 ج.م: Celin 500mg tab | 20 ج.م, Vitamin C Arrow tab | 10 ج.م, Redoxon C tab | 35 ج.م
drugInteractions:
❌ Iron + Antacids: Iron absorption significantly reduced — take iron 2 hours apart
❌ Iron + Tetracycline / Doxycycline: Iron chelates tetracyclines — separate by 3 hours
❌ Iron + Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin, Levofloxacin): Chelation reduces antibiotic absorption
❌ Iron + Levothyroxine: Iron impairs thyroid hormone absorption — take 4 hours apart
⚠️ Iron + PPIs: Reduced gastric acid decreases iron absorption — may need IV iron
⚠️ Iron + Milk / Tea / Coffee: Tannins and calcium reduce absorption — avoid with iron dose
✅ Iron + Vitamin C: Enhances absorption — recommended combination
